issue_context.title: 404 error for requests with invalid uri encoding
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure it has not already been reported


### Fastify version

3.17.0

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

14.16

### Operating system

macOS

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

11.4

### Description

when receiving a http request that contains invalid url encoding I get the following log output

```
07:48:34 ✨ incoming request GET xxx /%C0
07:48:34 ⚠️  the default handler for 404 did not catch this, this is likely a fastify bug, please report it
07:48:34 ⚠️  └── / (ACL)
    / (BIND)
    / (CHECKOUT)
    / (CONNECT)
    / (COPY)
    / (DELETE)
    / (GET)
    / (HEAD)
...
```

As stated in #1884, the result should actually be a 400 and we should not log errors to the log.

### Steps to Reproduce

Setup an empty default project
```bash
mkdir my-app
cd my-app
npm init fastify
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then send the following request (e.g. via `httpie`)
```bash
http 'localhost:3000/%c0'
```

### Expected Behavior

The server should return a 400 and not log errors to the log.
comments: This might be a bug in find-my-way
The bug is that the request is apparently caught by the not found handler of the not found handler. This should not be possible.
To clarify, throwing `404` is the expected result, but we should not fire the `fourOhFourFallBack` and it should be properly handled by `fastify`. Is that right?

### Symptom
1. Not registered any route will trigger this behavior
2. Regitered only `/` route will trigger this behavior

### Problem Breakdown
1 . `fastify` build route in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/fastify.js#L166)
2 . it register default route in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/fastify.js#L563-L568)
3 . which will look up the `fourOhFour` route in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/fastify.js#L179)
~4 . it will fallback to the default route in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/fourOhFour.js#L40)~
~5 . which will be the handler of [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/lib/fourOhFour.js#L154-L170)~
6 . as we call empty setNotFoundHandler in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/fastify.js#L381)
7 . we should be registered a `basic404` for `/*` in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/lib/fourOhFour.js#L107-L112)
8 . as a result, step 4 and step 5 should never reached

### Routing Flow
When invalid route reached `fastify`
1. reach normal router
2. reach `fourOhFour` router
3. calling `Router.prototype.lookup`
4. go to `wildcard route` handling
5. break in [here](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/master/index.js#L481-L485)
6. default handler is used [here](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/master/index.js#L344)

### Reason behind
`fourOhFour` router do not have `onBadUrl` handler passed in and `find-my-way` will break when both `url is invalid` and `onBadUrl` is not exist.
As a result, no route is actually reached and the `/*` route registered for `basic404` is not reached as well. 
Then, it will fallback to the default route in [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/lib/fourOhFour.js#L154-L170)

### Potential Fix
@mcollina @Eomm 
I think the fix should be add `onBadUrl` handler to `fourOhFour` router? It may have side effect of all invalid url cannot not reach `404`.

> I think the fix should be add `onBadUrl` handler to `fourOhFour` router? It may have side effect of all invalid url cannot not reach `404`.

Thanks for the analysis, this is correct! Good job. Would you send a PR?

We might ship this as a semver-major change.
